definition: ClothOff is a website that enables users to create deepfake pornography of women and girls by uploading non-pornographic photos and applying the website's generative artificial intelligence tools.
details: The website charges a fee for creation of these images. It is operated by AI/Robotics Venture Strategy 3 Ltd, a company incorporated in the British Virgin Islands with employees in Russia, Belarus, and Ukraine. ClothOff has been involved in controversies and lawsuits related to its users' generated images, especially because the website has enabled creation of non-consensual intimate imagery of minors, despite the company saying that is prohibited.

explainer.lead: ClothOff is a paid website whose generative AI turns ordinary photos into fabricated pornographic images of women and girls. It matters because the people depicted need not consent, and the service has faced controversies and lawsuits over generated imagery, including imagery of minors despite a stated ban.

tiers.eli5: Imagine someone pasting your face into a made-up picture and pretending it really shows you; ClothOff uses AI to make that kind of fake sexual image. It charges users to turn ordinary photos into fake pornography. This can deeply hurt the person pictured, especially when they never agreed or are a child.
tiers.practitioner: From an engineering perspective, ClothOff provides a paid generative-image workflow: an ordinary photograph is uploaded, processed by the website's generative AI, and used to create a fabricated pornographic image. The central pitfalls are consent and safety rather than image quality. Its stated prohibition on imagery of minors has not prevented users from creating non-consensual intimate imagery of minors.
tiers.paperLevel: Let x be a non-pornographic input photograph; ClothOff implements a paid generative mapping f(x) = y, where y is a synthetic pornographic depiction of a woman or girl. A documented limitation is the gap between policy and enforcement: imagery of minors is prohibited, yet users have generated non-consensual intimate imagery of minors.

explainer.example: A user uploads an ordinary clothed photograph of a woman and pays the creation fee. ClothOff generates a fake pornographic image of her even though she never posed for it or consented to its creation.

usedIn.name: Deepfake pornography
usedIn.detail: Generating fabricated sexual images from non-pornographic photographs.

usedIn.name: Non-consensual intimate imagery
usedIn.detail: Producing sexualized depictions without the depicted person's consent, including imagery of minors.

explainer.intuition: ClothOff treats an ordinary photograph as input to an image-generation service and produces a sexualized fabrication rather than recovering anything real. A fee is charged for creating the images.
howItWorks: A user supplies a non-pornographic photograph.
The website processes it with generative AI tools.
The system creates a fabricated pornographic depiction.
The user pays for image creation.
explainer.whyItMatters: The service makes non-consensual sexual fabrication accessible for a fee, creating serious risks for women and girls. Its controversies and lawsuits also show that a written prohibition on imagery of minors does not by itself prevent abuse.
misconceptions: The output is not a recovered or authentic nude photograph; it is generated.
A stated ban on imagery of minors does not mean such imagery cannot be created.
